academic_translation:
Without being angry at bile and the like,
Which are great sources of suffering,
Why be angry at beings with a mind?
They too are all incited by conditions.
translation: Things like bile cause great suffering, but we do not get angry at them. So why get angry at a being with a mind? They are also pushed by circumstances.

academic_translation:
For example, even without wishing it,
Just as this sickness arises,
Likewise, even without wishing it,
The afflictions forcefully arise.
translation: For example, sickness happens even when we do not want it. In the same way, troubling emotions rise up with force even when we do not want them.

academic_translation:
Even without thinking, "I shall become angry,"
People become angry at the slightest condition;
Even without thinking, "I shall produce it,"
Anger likewise arises.
translation: People get angry over little things without even thinking, "I will get angry." In the same way, anger just happens without us deciding to make it.

academic_translation:
All faults, however many there are,
And various kinds of misdeeds,
All these arise through the power of conditions;
They do not possess independence.
translation: Every single fault and all kinds of harmful deeds happen because of circumstances. They do not have independence.

academic_translation:
Even those assembled conditions
Have no intention, "I shall produce,"
And that which is produced by them
Has no intention, "I am produced."
translation: Even those circumstances that come together do not think, "I will make this happen." And the thing they make does not think, "I am being made."

academic_translation:
Whatever is asserted as "Pradhāna,"
And whatever is imputed as the "self,"
Do not arise by purposefully thinking,
"I shall come into being."
translation: Whatever people call Primal Matter, and whatever people call the self, do not decide to exist. They do not think, "I will come to be."

academic_translation:
If it does not exist when unarisen,
At that time, what wishes to arise?
Since it would constantly be distracted by sense objects,
It would also never cease.
translation: If it does not exist before it begins, what could wish to exist? Because it would always be busy with things we sense, it could never stop.

academic_translation:
If that self is permanent,
It is evidently inactive, like space.
Even if it encounters other conditions,
What can be done to the unchanging?
translation: If that self is lasting forever, it clearly does nothing, just like space. Even if it meets other circumstances, what can change something that never changes?

academic_translation:
If, even at the time of acting, it remains as before,
What has the action done to it?
What connection could there be
By which one could say, "This is its action"?
translation: If something stays exactly the same while it acts, what did the action do to it? What connection could there be? How could anyone say, "This is its action"?

academic_translation:
Thus, everything is under the power of others,
And through that power, it is powerless.
Knowing this, one will not become angry
At any entities, which are like emanations.
translation: So, everything is controlled by other forces. Because of this power, everything is powerless. Knowing this, I will not get angry at any things. They are just like magic illusions.

academic_translation:
If you object, "By what is what to be prevented?
Even preventing is unreasonable!"
In dependence upon that, it is not unreasonable
To wish for sufferings to be severed.
translation: Someone might ask, "What can stop what? Even stopping things makes no sense!" But because things depend on each other, it does make sense. It is not wrong to wish for sufferings to be cut away.

academic_translation:
Therefore, whether it is an enemy or a friend,
If you see them doing what is improper,
Thinking, "This has arisen from such conditions,"
Reflect in this way and remain at ease.
translation: Therefore, whether it is an enemy or a friend, if I see them doing something wrong, I will think, "This has come from these circumstances." I will think this way and stay at ease.

academic_translation:
If things were accomplished by their own will,
Since no one desires suffering,
For all embodied beings,
Suffering would not arise for anyone.
translation: If things happened just by their own choice, suffering would never happen to anyone. Since no one wants suffering, it would never arise for any beings with a body.

academic_translation:
Through heedlessness, they even harm themselves
With thorns and so forth;
In order to obtain women and the like,
They grow vehement and engage in fasting and so forth.
translation: Through carelessness, people even hurt themselves with thorns and other things. To get women and other things they want, they get very worked up and start going without food.

academic_translation:
Some hang themselves or leap from cliffs,
Eat poison and unwholesome food,
And through non-meritorious conduct,
Bring harm upon themselves.

locked_terms.use: way of acting that builds no store of goodness

translation: Some people hang themselves or jump off cliffs. They eat poison and bad food. They bring harm to themselves through a way of acting that builds no store of goodness.

academic_translation:
When, under the power of afflictions,
They even kill their beloved selves,
At that time, how could they not cause harm
To the bodies of others?
translation: When people are controlled by a troubling emotion, they might even kill themselves. If they can hurt themselves like this, how could they not hurt others?

academic_translation:
For those who, through the arising of afflictions,
Engage in such acts as killing themselves,
If compassion does not even arise,
What sense is there in anger?
translation: A troubling emotion can make people do terrible things like killing themselves. If compassion does not even arise for them, what sense is there in anger?

academic_translation:
If causing harm to others
Is the nature of childish ones,
It is inappropriate to feel anger toward them,
Like resenting fire for its nature to burn.
translation: If hurting others is just the nature of a childish person, it is wrong to feel anger toward them. That would be like being mad at fire because its nature is to burn.

academic_translation:
Alternatively, if this fault is adventitious,
And the nature of sentient beings is gentle,
Even then it is inappropriate to feel anger,
Like resenting the sky when smoke rises within it.
translation: Or what if this bad behavior is only temporary, and the nature of living beings is gentle? Even then, it is wrong to feel anger. That would be like being mad at the sky just because smoke rises in it.

academic_translation:
Having employed sticks and the like as the actual instruments,
if one feels anger at the one who throws them,
since he too is driven by hatred,
then, in the second place, it is fitting to feel anger at hatred.
translation: Someone might hit me with a stick. If I feel anger at the person swinging it, I must remember they are driven by hatred. It makes more sense to feel anger at hatred itself.

academic_translation:
In the past, to sentient beings,
I inflicted harm such as this;
Therefore, upon me, a harmer of sentient beings,
It is fitting that this harm should arise.
translation: In the past, I hurt living beings like this. Because I harmed living beings, it is only right that I get hurt now.

academic_translation:
His weapon and my body,
both are causes of suffering;
since he has drawn the weapon and I have taken up the body,
at whom should I direct my anger?
translation: His weapon and my body are both causes of suffering. He brought the weapon, and I brought my body. So who should get my anger?

academic_translation:
Like a human-shaped abscess,
Full of suffering, unable to bear being touched,
Since I, blinded by craving, have grasped it,
When it is harmed, at whom should I direct my anger?
translation: This body is like a painful sore shaped like a person. It is full of suffering and hurts to touch. Blinded by wanting, I held onto it. When it gets hurt, who should get my anger?

academic_translation:
Childish ones do not desire suffering,
yet they crave the causes of suffering;
when harmed by their own faults,
what grounds are there to blame others?
translation: A childish person does not want suffering. But they still want the causes of suffering. When they are hurt by their own mistakes, why should they blame others?

academic_translation:
For example, like hell guardians,
And the forest of sword-leaves,
Since this is produced by my own karma,
At whom should I direct my anger?
translation: Think of the hell guardians and the forest of sword leaves. My own actions made them appear. So who should get my anger?

academic_translation:
Impelled by my own karma,
Those who harm me appear;
If because of this those beings go to hell,
Have I not ruined them?
translation: Pushed by my own actions, people appear and hurt me. If doing this makes them go to hell, haven't I ruined them?

academic_translation:
By relying upon them,
Through patience my many misdeeds are purified;
But by relying upon me, they
Go to the hells of long-lasting suffering.
translation: Because of them, I practice patience. This wipes away my many harmful deeds. But because of me, they go to the hells. They face long-lasting suffering there.

academic_translation:
I am the one who harms them,
While they are the ones who benefit me;
Why, out of perversity,
O wicked mind, do you give rise to anger?
translation: I am the one who harms them. They are the ones who help me. O wicked mind, why do you act in such a mistaken way? Why do you create anger?

academic_translation:
If I possess the intention's
Good quality, I will not go to hell;
If I protect myself,
What will happen to them here?
translation: If my intention has a good quality, I will not go to hell. But if I just protect myself, what will happen to them?

academic_translation:
But if I cause harm in return,
They will not be protected,
And my conduct will also decline;
Thus my austerity will be destroyed.
translation: If I harm them back, they will not be safe. My good way of acting will get worse. Then my hard practice will be ruined.

academic_translation:
Because the mind is not an embodied being,
No one can destroy it anywhere;
Due to fixation on the body,
The body is harmed by sufferings.
translation: The mind is not a being with a body. Because of this, no one can destroy it anywhere. But by holding on tightly to the body, the body is hurt by sufferings.

academic_translation:
Contempt, speaking harsh speech,
And those unpleasant words—
Since they do not harm the body,
O mind, why do you react with intense anger?
translation: Disrespect, harsh words, and unpleasant talk do not harm the body. O mind, why do you feel such strong anger?

academic_translation:
If others' displeasure with me
Will not consume me
In this life or some other life,
Why am I averse to it?
translation: If other people being upset with me will not destroy me in this life or another life, why do I dislike it?

academic_translation:
If I am averse to this
Because it creates an obstacle to gain,
My gain will be discarded here,
But my misdeeds will remain steadfast.
translation: If I dislike this because it puts something in the way of my gain, my gain will just be left behind here. But my harmful deeds will stay firmly with me.

academic_translation:
It is better that I die this very day
Than to live a long time through wrong livelihood;
Even if I were to remain for a long time,
The suffering of death is exactly the same.

locked_terms.use: wrong way to earn a living

translation: It is better to die today than to live a long time through a wrong way to earn a living. Even if I stay alive for a long time, the suffering of death is exactly the same.

academic_translation:
Whoever awakens
After experiencing happiness in a dream for a hundred years,
And another who awakens
After experiencing happiness for just an instant—
translation: Think of a person who wakes up after enjoying happiness in a dream for a hundred years. Think of another person who wakes up after enjoying happiness for just one moment.

academic_translation:
For both of those who awaken,
That happiness does not return;
For both a long life and a short life,
At the time of death, it is exactly the same.
translation: For both of the people who wake up, that happiness does not return. For both a long life and a short life, it is exactly the same at the time of death.

academic_translation:
Even if I acquire abundant gain,
And enjoy happiness for a long time,
Just like someone robbed by a thief,
I will depart naked and empty-handed.
translation: Even if I get a lot of gain and enjoy happiness for a long time, I will leave naked and empty-handed. I will be just like someone robbed by a thief.

academic_translation:
If I say, "By surviving on gain,
I will exhaust misdeeds and create merit,"
If I feel anger for the sake of gain,
Will merit not be exhausted and misdeeds arise?
translation: I might say, "By staying alive through gain, I will wipe out harmful deeds and build a store of goodness." But if I feel anger to get that gain, won't my store of goodness run out? Won't more harmful deeds happen?

academic_translation:
The very purpose for which I live—
If it is itself destroyed,
What is the use of that life
That commits only misdeeds?
translation: If the very reason I live is destroyed, what is the point of living? What good is a life that only does harmful deeds?
